name: modularsynth-mcp

tools.name: describe_patch
tools.description: Describe the current patch in the ModularSynth rack: modules (id, type, settings, "bypass": true when bypassed), cables ("moduleId:port" → "moduleId:port"), polyphony, whether the clock is running, and "editing": the Note Grid the user has open in its editor right now (write there when they talk about "the notes"). Call it first.

tools.name: list_module_types
tools.description: List the module types you can add, with their inputs, outputs and settings (name, label shown on the panel, min, max, default, unit; "options": the meaning of each value of a selector, from min upward). Pass a type to get just that one. Audio and control signals are voltages: pitch is 1 V per octave (0 V = C4), gates are 0/10 V. Drums can be synthesized with modules, the modular way (kick: a sine VCO whose pitch drops fast, through a VCA with a short envelope; snare: noise through a band-pass VCF with a brief envelope; hi-hat: noise high-passed, very short — see the "Noise percussion" preset), or played by samplers from the built-in kit (list_sounds, set_sample) for a quick result; both are triggered by a Trigger Seq. Choose from what the user asks for. Real instruments and voices (saxophone, vocals…) can’t be synthesized convincingly: use a sampler with a recording the user drops on it (or one of their saved sounds), or audioin (the user’s microphone or line input).

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List the ready-made presets (name and what they do). Load one with load_preset to start from a working sound.

tools.name: load_preset
tools.description: Replace the rack with a ready-made preset, by name (see list_presets). The user can undo it.

tools.name: new_patch
tools.description: Replace the rack with the default starter patch (keyboard → oscillator → filter → amplifier → output). The user can undo it.

tools.name: add_module
tools.description: Add a module to the rack. Optional row and x (in HP) place it; otherwise it goes to the first free spot. Optional params set its knobs. Returns its id. Drums: synthesize them with modules (VCO, Noise, VCF, ADSR, VCA) or load the built-in kit into samplers with set_sample. For a real instrument or a voice, a sampler with the user’s recording, or audioin for a microphone.

tools.name: remove_module
tools.description: Remove a module and its cables from the rack.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Patch a cable from an output to an input, both written "moduleId:port". An input takes one cable: plugging into a busy input replaces its cable.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Unplug the cable going into an input ("moduleId:port").

tools.name: set_param
tools.description: Turn a knob or flip a switch on a module. The value is clamped to the setting range; the value actually set is returned.

tools.name: nudge_param
tools.description: Turn a knob up or down by a little, some (default) or a lot, along the knob's own travel (logarithmic for frequencies and times), never past its range — for relative requests: "brighter" (filter cutoff up), "darker", "faster" (clock bpm up), "more reverb" (mix up). The old and new values are returned.

tools.name: set_bypass
tools.description: Bypass a module (on: true) or turn it back on (on: false), without unplugging anything: effects and processors (filters, VCA, mixers, delay, reverb…) pass their input straight through; sources and modulators (oscillators, LFO, envelopes, sequencers, clock…) go silent. Output, Scope and Memo can’t be bypassed. Useful to hear a part of a rich patch more clearly; the user can undo it.

tools.name: set_notes
tools.description: Write the notes of one page (A–D, default A) of a Note Grid sequencer; the other pages are kept. Each note: start step (0–63: sixteenth notes when clocked by Clock ×4, thirty-second notes when the Note Grid "resolution" setting is 1), length in steps, MIDI pitch (60 = C4), optional velocity. Replaces the notes of that page. Only the page selected by the "page" setting plays: put a verse on A and a chorus on B, then save scenes with different "page" values.

tools.name: set_steps
tools.description: Write the steps of a sequencer in one call. Trigger Seq: "tracks", each a track (1–4) and a pattern of up to 16 characters, "x" a hit and "." a rest (e.g. "x...x...x...x..." four on the floor), on page A–D (default: the page the module shows); the other tracks are kept, and written tracks leave Euclidean mode. Step Seq: "notes", up to 16 MIDI pitches (60 = C4) or null for a silent step; the length follows, and each pitch is fitted to the module's scale and octave range (from C4 up), so the notes actually set are returned. For a Note Grid, use set_notes.

tools.name: set_voices
tools.description: Set the polyphony of the patch: how many notes can sound at once (1–16). Chords from a keyboard or a Note Grid need as many voices as notes; a mono bass or lead sounds best with 1.

tools.name: transform_notes
tools.description: Transform one page (A–D, default: the page the module shows) of a Note Grid: "harmonize" adds the third (voices "third", default) or the third and fifth ("third+fifth") of the scale above each note; "humanize" varies velocities (and start times by one step at 1/32 resolution) by "amount" (0–1, default 0.5); "vary" copies the page to page "to" (default the next page) and moves about amount×30 % of the notes to a neighbouring scale note — a quick variation for a chorus or a break. Scale: "scale" and "root" (0 = C … 11 = B; scale indexes as in list_module_types for the Quant module), otherwise guessed from the notes.

tools.name: play_notes
tools.description: Play notes live, as if on the keyboard (the patch must have a MIDI→CV module wired to sound, its KEYBOARD screen set to All or Computer). Each note: MIDI pitch (60 = C4), start and duration in seconds from now, optional velocity. Up to 64 notes within 30 seconds.

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Save the current settings and sequences of every module as a scene (like a snapshot: intro, verse, chorus, break…), or overwrite an existing scene. Up to 16 scenes. Tempo and the clock's run state are not part of scenes. Returns the scene id.

tools.name: recall_scene
tools.description: Switch to a saved scene, like pressing its button: on the next bar while the sound plays, right away otherwise. Stops the song if it was playing.

tools.name: set_song
tools.description: Write the song: scenes played one after another, each for a number of bars (e.g. intro 4, verse 8, chorus 8, break 4, chorus 8). Up to 64 lines; an empty list removes the song. "loop": start again at the end (default true; otherwise the clocks stop). Needs a Clock in the patch to count bars.

tools.name: play_song
tools.description: Play the song from its first line (or from line "from", counted from 0): the scene of each line plays for its bars, clocks restart on the first beat. Stop it with set_transport running: false.

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Listen to the patch for a few seconds (default 2, up to 10) and report what actually sounds: for each Output module, its peak level in dBFS and whether the master limiter is squeezing it (too loud: lower a level or the Output gain); the peak voltage of every module output; and which modules are silent. Use it after building or changing a patch, with the clock running for sequenced parts, to check that it makes sound and is not too loud. Needs audio on.

tools.name: look
tools.description: See the synth: with no argument, a photo of the whole rack (modules, knob positions, cables); with "module", that module's panel plus an oscilloscope and spectrum of one of its outputs ("port", default the first output); with "output": true, the oscilloscope and spectrum of what reaches the Output. Use it to check a patch visually: a clipped or silent waveform, a filter closed too far, a bass that fills the spectrum. Scope and spectrum need audio on.

tools.name: show_player
tools.description: Show the ModularSynth player in the conversation (in apps that support MCP Apps): the patch name, play/stop and up to 6 knobs you choose ("moduleId:setting", the ones that matter most for this sound), so the user can play with them without leaving the chat. Call it when you have finished a patch. The sound still comes from the ModularSynth tab.

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Show the user a module, a knob or a jack by making it glow in the rack for a few seconds (the rack scrolls to it). target: "moduleId", "moduleId:setting" or "moduleId:port". With "to" (an input "moduleId:port") and an output as target, it draws the cable to plug as a dotted line. Use it when you explain or ask the user to turn or patch something.

tools.name: list_sounds
tools.description: List the sounds a sampler can play: the built-in starter kit (kick, snare, hi-hat, a chord, a pad — always available, made by the synth itself) and the user’s own sounds saved in this browser. Load one with set_sample.

tools.name: set_sample
tools.description: Load a sound (an id from list_sounds) into a sampler module. Then trigger it with its gate input (from a Trigger Seq, a Note Grid or MIDI→CV) and choose how it plays with set_param "mode": 0 one-shot (drums), 1 hold (plays while the gate is high), 2 loop (synced to the clock).

tools.name: set_transport
tools.description: Start or stop every Clock in the patch (the ▶/■ button): sequencers play while it runs. Stopping also stops a playing song.

tools.name: what_changed
tools.description: What the user (and other assistants) changed in the patch since your last action: knobs turned, cables patched, modules added, scenes recalled, the clock started. Every tool answer already ends with this when something changed; call this to look again, for example when the user says "your turn" after playing — then answer what they did, like a musician would.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change (yours or the user’s), like Ctrl+Z: first cancels a scene waiting for the next bar, stops a playing song.

instructions:
ModularSynth is a modular synthesizer running in the user's browser tab. You build and play patches with these tools; the user hears the result and can undo every change with Ctrl+Z.

How to work:
- Call describe_patch first, and list_module_types (with a type) before using a module you don't know.
- Signals are voltages: pitch is 1 V per octave (0 V = C4), gates and triggers are 0/10 V, audio is about ±5 V.
- After building or changing something, check it: listen (levels at the Output, limiter, silent modules) and look (rack photo, a module's panel, oscilloscope and spectrum). Start the clock first for sequenced parts. Audio must be on: if it is off, ask the user to click the audio button in the top bar.
- Drums: synthesize them with modules (kick: sine VCO whose pitch drops fast into a VCA with a short envelope; snare: noise through a band-pass VCF; hi-hat: high-passed noise, very short), or load the built-in kit into samplers (list_sounds, set_sample). Real instruments and voices: a sampler with the user's recording, or audioin.
- Relative requests ("brighter", "faster", "more reverb", "a bit less"): nudge_param turns a knob up or down along its own travel.
- Sequencers: set_steps (Trigger Seq patterns, Step Seq notes), set_notes and transform_notes (Note Grid). Chords need as many voices as notes (set_voices).
- Playing together: every answer ends with what the user changed since your last action. When the user says "your turn" or plays something, call what_changed and answer musically.
- show_player shows a small player in the conversation when the app supports it.
